what: UV, sunlight at the ground, clear-sky days and haze for every area, by month, for the place card.
service: NASA POWER, POWER Climatology API (version in each parameter's answers), regional endpoint, community RE

areas.order: the order of ids in site/data/cells.json

layout.how_to_read: the value of area i, field k, month j (0 = January) is the uint16 at byte offset 2 * ((i * 6 + k) * 12 + j); divide by divide_by[field]; 65535 = unknown, never 0

uv_index.grid: 1 x 1 degree boxes (centres at x.5 degrees), read from each answer. This is the CERES SYN1deg grid.
uv_index.what_it_is_source_words: The UV index at the ground under the real sky, cloudy or clear, as a monthly mean. It is UV light weighted by how strongly it burns skin, in W per square metre, times 40.
uv_index.what_it_is_not_source_words: Not the noon or peak UV index that weather services publish. The service's daily value is the mean of all 24 hours (meta.checks.uv_index_daily_value). At two boxes over ten summer days it equalled the hourly mean within 0.003. There the brightest hour was 2.3 to 2.4 times larger. Not a value at one spot: a box about 111 km tall. Not UV on the Moon, which has no air and no ozone to filter it.

sun_kwh_m2_day.name_in_the_service: All Sky Surface Shortwave Downward Irradiance
sun_kwh_m2_day.definition_in_the_service: The total solar irradiance incident (direct plus diffuse) on a horizontal plane at the surface of the earth under all sky conditions. An alternative term for the total solar irradiance is the "Global Horizontal Irradiance" or GHI.
sun_kwh_m2_day.unit_words: kilowatt-hours per square metre per day
sun_kwh_m2_day.grid: 1 x 1 degree boxes (centres at x.5 degrees), read from each answer. This is the CERES SYN1deg grid.
sun_kwh_m2_day.what_it_is_source_words: All solar energy, direct plus diffuse, reaching a level surface per day under the real sky. A monthly mean: the global horizontal irradiance.
sun_kwh_m2_day.what_it_is_not_source_words: Not what a tilted or Sun-tracking panel would get. With the Sun low, a vertical panel facing it gets much more than a level one. Not a panel's output, and not the light of the low-Sun hours only: it is the whole day's total.

sun_clear_kwh_m2_day.name_in_the_service: Clear Sky Surface Shortwave Downward Irradiance
sun_clear_kwh_m2_day.definition_in_the_service: The total solar irradiance incident (direct plus diffuse) on a horizontal plane at the surface of the earth under clear sky conditions. An alternative term for the total solar irradiance is the "Global Horizontal Irradiance" or GHI.
sun_clear_kwh_m2_day.unit_words: kilowatt-hours per square metre per day
sun_clear_kwh_m2_day.grid: 1 x 1 degree boxes (centres at x.5 degrees), read from each answer. This is the CERES SYN1deg grid.
sun_clear_kwh_m2_day.what_it_is_source_words: The same solar energy on a level surface per day as if there were no cloud, monthly mean. The air and its aerosol stay in place.
sun_clear_kwh_m2_day.what_it_is_not_source_words: Not a measurement on clear days: it is a computed clear-sky value for every day.

clear_days.definition_in_the_service: The number of Clear Sky Days if the daytime cloud amount is less than 10 percent.
clear_days.grid: 1 x 1 degree boxes (centres at x.5 degrees), read from each answer. This is the CERES SYN1deg grid.
clear_days.what_it_is_source_words: The service's count of days whose daytime cloud over the grid box is under 10 percent. It is added up over all the years, so it reaches 355 in one January. The field clear_days divides it by the years that checks.period found it covers.
clear_days.what_it_is_not_source_words: Not days in a typical month until divided by the years, as clear_days does. Not the hours a camera can see the Sun or the ground. A day with 15 percent cloud counts as not clear; a clear spell of a few hours is not counted. In months without sunlight the service still counts clear days by its cloud rule. A count there says nothing about seeing by sunlight. A box about 111 km tall is under 10 percent cloud on fewer days than one spot in it.
clear_days.how: the service's count summed over the years, divided by the number of years

aod_550.definition_in_the_service: The adjusted optical thickness at 0.55 um measured vertically; the component of the atmosphere to quantify the removal of radiant energy from an incident beam.
aod_550.grid: 1 x 1 degree boxes (centres at x.5 degrees), read from each answer. This is the CERES SYN1deg grid.
aod_550.what_it_is_source_words: Aerosol optical depth at 550 nm, monthly mean, as the service adjusts it. It says how much fine particles in the whole air column dim a vertical beam of green light. A value of 0.1 dims it by about 10 percent.
aod_550.what_it_is_not_source_words: Not dust alone: all fine particles together, such as mineral dust, smoke, sea salt and sulphate haze. Not dust on the ground, not blowing grit, and nothing like lunar regolith dust. The service's climatology list holds no dust-only figure. It is served to two decimals, so 0.0 means under 0.005, not an empty sky. In months without sunlight the service still gives a number; how it makes it then was not checked.

cloud_day_pct_fallback.unit_words: percent of the sky, daylight hours
cloud_day_pct_fallback.rule: stored only in a month whose clear-day count is unknown; unknown everywhere else

groups.heading: Surface sunlight
groups.unit_words: kilowatt-hours per square metre per day
groups.label_words: the solar energy that gets to level ground in a day, for the real sky; the clear-sky figure is next to it
is: The solar energy that gets to level ground in a day, direct plus diffuse, under the real mix of cloud and clear sky.
The clear-sky figure is a calculation without cloud.
is_not: It is not the energy that a tilted panel, or a panel that faces the Sun, gets. It is not the output of a panel.
It is the total for a full day, not the light in the hours of low Sun.

connecting-ridge: There is no air to make the sunlight less bright or to scatter it before it gets to the ground.
As a mean over the mapped area, the ground at Connecting Ridge is in sunlight for approximately 29 percent of the time.
Our data does not have the energy per day on the lunar surface.

groups.heading: UV index
groups.label_words: the mean of all 24 hours, not the noon peak
is: The UV index at the ground under the real sky, as a mean of all 24 hours of the day.
is_not: It is not the noon peak that a forecast gives.
We checked two boxes over ten days in summer. There, the brightest hour was 2.3 to 2.4 times the 24-hour mean.
moon: The Moon has no air (surface pressure approximately 3 × 10⁻¹⁵ bar at night) and no ozone. Thus, nothing filters the UV there, and this includes UVC.
Our data has no UV figure for the Moon.

groups.heading: Clear-sky days
groups.label_words: the days in a month when the daytime cloud over the whole grid box is less than 10 percent
groups.fallback_words: The service gave no count of clear days here. Thus, this figure is the daytime cloud amount.
is: The days in a month when the daytime cloud over the whole grid box is less than 10 percent.
The service gives the total count for all the years. At the boxes that we checked, this total agrees with 20 years (2001 to 2020). Thus, we divide by 20.
is_not: It is not the hours that a camera can see. A day with some cloud over the box is not a clear day.
In months without sunlight, the count does not tell what you can see by sunlight.
moon: The Moon has no air (surface pressure approximately 3 × 10⁻¹⁵ bar at night). Thus, it has no cloud, and each day there is free of cloud.

groups.heading: Haze
groups.unit_words: aerosol optical depth at 550 nm, no unit
groups.label_words: all fine particles in the air, not only dust
is: Aerosol optical depth at 550 nm: how much the fine particles in the full column of air decrease the sunlight.
is_not: It is all fine particles in the air, not only dust. It includes dust, smoke, sea salt and haze together.
It does not tell about dust on the ground. The service has no figure for dust only.
The service gives it to two decimals. Thus, 0.00 means less than 0.005.
moon: The Moon has no air to hold particles. Its dust is on the ground.
The dust is dry regolith with sharp grains, because no water or air made them round. It sticks to suits and equipment.

tag: NASA POWER, monthly mean on a coarse grid
general: Each figure is a monthly mean for a grid box approximately 111 km from north to south. It is not a measurement at the area.
Many areas are in one grid box. Thus, areas that are near each other often show the same figures.
The service gives the years 2001 to 2025. But at the boxes that we checked, its values agree better with 2001 to 2020.
Each figure is a mean for the full day. No figure is for the hours of low Sun only.
No score or ranking uses these figures.
A month without sunlight shows a true zero for sunlight and UV.
The page shows the figures to two decimals. Thus, 0.00 can be a value less than 0.005.

strip.caption: Drawn by code from open data; the code was written with AI assistance.
strip.sunless_words: A tinted band shows the months without sunlight.
strip.best_words: A mark shows the months of the best ten-day periods.
strip.scale_words: Each strip uses one scale for all areas. Thus, you can compare two places.
strip.step_fallback_words: This area has no terrain hours. Thus, the best periods come from snow-free ground.
strip.no_best_words: No ten-day period has hours for this lunar region. Thus, the card shows the full year.
strip.list_note: clear days a month in the best month

sunless_rule: a month whose clear-sky sunlight (sun_clear_kwh_m2_day) is a known 0 has no sunlight at the area's grid box

clear_days_fallback.words: The service gave no count of clear days here. Thus, this figure is the daytime cloud amount.

unknown: 65535 in environment.bin and null here: never 0
not_checked: how CERES SYN1deg makes its aerosol and UV values (the service names SYN1DEG; nothing else was read)
the hours of low Sun: every value is a whole-day or monthly mean
